 Judgment

Claimant in OP(MV) No.339/2016 of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manjeri [hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal'] has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal as claimant and respondents.

3. Claimant filed the OP seeking compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act stating that on 27.10.2015, at about 10 AM while he was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KL-71/A-554,
a car bearing number KL-47/E-8282 driven by respondent No.1 hit on the motorcycle and as a result of which, the claimant sustained serious injuries.
The first respondent is the owner-cum-driver of the car and the 2nd respondent is its insurer.
4. After trial, the Tribunal awarded a sum of 5,77,500/- as compensation with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

5. Dissatisfied with the amount awarded, the claimant has come up in appeal contending that the amount awarded is inadequate;that the notional income of 10,500/- per month taken MACA NO.
3239 OF 2019 2026:KER:29373 for assessing the compensation is very low; that the Tribunal has not awarded just and reasonable compensation as mandated by law and therefore, he seeks enhancement of the compensation.
6. Heard the learned counsel for both sides.
Records perused.

7. Claimant's case is that in the accident he sustained degloving injury 10x4 cm back of right elbow,
front of right wrist and hand with cut ulnar nerve bundle, flexor carpi ulnaris with loss of 3 cms nerve and he was treated as inpatient for 7 days.
He has produced the medical records which would reveal the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
The Medical Board has issued Ext.X1 disability certificate to the effect that he sustained permanent disability of 13% due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
8. The Tribunal calculated the compensation by taking notional income as 10,500/- per month.
9. The specific case of the claimant who was then aged 29 years is that he was a Coolie and was earning 12,000/- per month.
10. The Tribunal has awarded loss of earnings for 5 months at the rate of 10,500/- per month.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, I find it appropriate to take a period of 6 months for awarding compensation under the said head.
Accordingly, an amount of 63,000/- is awarded under the head loss of earnings [10,500x6].

sentences.text: 11. Under the head Extra Nourishment as against the claim of 4000/-, the Tribunal has awarded 2100/- which is on a lower side.
Accordingly, an additional sum of 1,900/- is awarded on that head.
12. Under the head damages to clothing, only an amount of Rs.750/- is seen awarded as against the claim of 1000/-.
Accordingly, an additional sum of 250/- is awarded under that head.
13. Under the head pain and suffering the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of 30,000/-.
Regard being had to the gravity of injuries, and the pain and sufferings he had to undergo, an additional sum of 15,000/- is awarded.
14. Under the head loss of amenities, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount.
Claimant has sustained serious injuries and he has sustained permanent disability of 13%.
Hence an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head loss of amenities.
15. In the result, appeal stands allowed.
